A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on label-generation probabilities, distribution alignment, linear probing, and supplementary mechanism analyses in Sections 4-5 and Appendices C-D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Qwen, Medusa, and label-order experiments in Appendices D.7-D.9.

M1.justification: The proposed compare-to-none, unary and binary breakdown, max-over-generations, and supervised procedures remain unchanged. The new token-variant explanation documents implementation choices without establishing a procedural change from v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use Boxes, SemEval, GoEmotions, MFRC, HateXplain, and MSP-Podcast with the same represented tasks and label coverage. Added model configurations and prompt-order controls extend experiments within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The tabulated alignment comparator set is unchanged. Section 5.2.2 newly reports trying Monte Carlo sampling and finding it noisier than analytical label probabilities, adding a limited qualitative comparison without corresponding numerical results.

E3.justification: Appendices D.7-D.9 add Qwen 2.5 7B/72B Base and Instruct configurations, Medusa Zephyr 7B with multiple decoding heads, and alphabetical, randomized, and reversed label-order controls. These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing alignment splits, sample counts, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether generation and probing findings generalize to Qwen, whether multiple decoding heads alter the behavior, and whether label ordering influences predictions. These address generalizability and a potential confound beyond the retained ablations and attention analyses.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly specifies three seeds for randomized label ordering, without establishing increased repetitions of existing experiments. Figure 5 removes the shaded bands present in v1; their statistical meaning was not specified. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds Qwen/Medusa results, annotation statistics, and label-order findings: Table 7 reports 96.4% alphabetical outputs with alphabetical prompts versus 35.2% with randomized prompts. Figure 5 adds traces and revises existing Llama accuracy values. The matched 70B and 8B alignment tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The multi-label distribution formulation, empirical human-distribution estimator, alignment mathematics, and Bradley-Terry objective remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and an added introduction contribution explicitly claim that max-over-generations improves alignment and F1 with no additional computation, strengthening v1's characterization of little additional computational overhead. The central sequential-prediction and distribution-alignment claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 identifies alphabetical and prompt-order priors as potential drivers of the observed behavior and suggests randomized-order aggregation. It also qualifies the older binary-calibration motivation and discusses generalization to Qwen/Medusa. Section 7 remains unchanged, including its now-inconsistent Llama-only limitation.

D1.justification: V2 discloses maximum-logit selection across equivalent label-token forms, the complete GoEmotions cluster membership and clustering basis, and checkpoint identifiers for Qwen and Medusa. Existing training and hardware details remain; the code link is merely relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Medusa, surface-form competition, and the Qwen technical report. It also clarifies that the cited binary-calibration evidence concerns older neural networks. The related-work structure and principal novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is revised, the introduction gains a contribution bullet, and Section 4 expands explanations of probability extraction and sequential comparisons. Appendices D.7-D.9 are appended, while the existing section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 replaces v1's linear-probing Table 2 with Figure 7, adds annotation and ordering tables, expands Figures 5-6, and introduces Qwen/Medusa Figures 13-16. These substantially extend the visual presentation; many earlier appendix figures are retained with renumbering or relocation.

improvement.justification: The Qwen/Medusa checks broaden support for the observed mechanisms, while the ordering control and token/clustering details improve transparency and reproducibility. These provide a net benefit, but the new ordering confound is not fully reconciled with the main causal interpretation, and Section 7 still describes a Llama-only study.
